summary.headline: V-Guard Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23.5% YoY to INR1,810 crore and EBITDA margin widened to 10.5% from 8.4%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 23.5% YoY to INR1,810 crore, with about 14% price and 9% volume contribution per management's blended split. EBITDA excluding other income rose 54.5% to INR191 crore, and PAT rose 76% to INR130 crore. Gross margin held at 36.9%, flat YoY, as management says roughly 75-80% of input cost inflation has been passed through. Management raised FY27 growth expectations to above 15% and reaffirmed a 9-10% EBITDA margin, while noting wires volumes were nearly flat under a large price increase.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR155 crore a year ago

segments.name: Electronics (stabilizers, UPS, solar)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 22.8% YoY with all major categories contributing; solar is growing fastest on a small base, and solar pumps for Maharashtra government are only a couple of crore so far.

segments.name: Electricals
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 27.7% YoY, aided by higher copper prices; wires saw very high price growth with near-flat volumes, while ex-wires grew at high double digits and switchgear, modular switches and pumps grew volumes robustly.

segments.name: Consumer Durables (fans, water heaters, kitchen, air coolers)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 19.2% YoY; induction cooktops spiked, other kitchen categories grew healthily, fans grew reasonably (pedestal fans short on inventory), and air coolers lost share due to weak North demand and competitor price delays.

segments.name: Sunflame
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 18.3% YoY on a low base; management says integration is complete and a sales acceleration programme has started, with margin recovery expected to be more gradual than top-line recovery.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected to be more than 15%, with management saying it may be 'a bit more than 15%' given price growth; no specific number given.
EBITDA margin to be maintained at 9-10% ('we should be okay this year in terms of margins').
Long-term target of 15% growth, with normal-year mix of 10-12% volume and 2-3% price growth.
Capex to average INR150-170 crore per year over the next two years, below the earlier INR200-250 crore range.
Advertising spend to reach about 2.5% of revenue for FY27, with spending resumed from around May 15.
Pricing actions about 80-85% complete; some smaller categories still need price increases in the current quarter, and management does not expect large further hikes.
Wires competitive intensity expected to slow growth for some unorganised-sector players by 1-2% vs market, with no major impact in the first one to two years.
capex_capacity: Capex guidance revised: INR150-170 crore per year on average for the next two years, versus the earlier INR200-250 crore range referenced by the analyst.
Own manufacturing now above 65% of products (previously sourced), a key driver of gross margin improvement.
Investment phase in capability (technology, systems, R&D, renewables, lighting) expected to last another two to three years before plateauing.
Lighting launch planned in FY27; solar rooftop next-generation battery (BESS) launch planned in the next two to three months.
Gegadyne (battery start-up) has moved from R&D to commercial supply to small customers; V-Guard may source batteries from it.
demand_pricing: Pricing: management cited a blended split of about 14% price and 9% volume within 22-23% revenue growth; category price increases range from 5% to 18%, with some categories cited up to 30%.
Wires: very large price increases led to near-zero volume growth as customers deferred purchases; value growth held up and margins were maintained.
Copper purchase mix shifted to roughly 95% domestic from 70-80% earlier, which helped working capital through supplier credit.
Management described the 12-14% price increase over four months as unprecedented since 2006 and said consumers have accepted it so far.
Air coolers lost share as some competitors delayed price increases and the North zone was weak.
Solar rooftop: focus is B2C residential and small SMEs; BESS seen as the next large opportunity at about INR1.5-2 lakh per home.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 22-23% growth is price vs volume, and how much of the input inflation has been passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended growth split is about 14% price and 9% volume; about 80-85% of pricing actions are complete and roughly 75-80% of inflation has been passed through, with the gross margin expected to hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why is South growing faster than non-South for the fourth quarter in a row?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes it mainly to weather: South had a good summer while North was disrupted by rain. It also said it took pricing ahead of competitors in non-South markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is the capex guidance still INR2-2.5 billion a year?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Capex is expected to average INR150-170 crore a year over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth and margins be higher than the medium-term guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth is expected to be more than 15%, with the 15% figure kept as the long-term aim. EBITDA margin is expected at 9-10%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is payables so high on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a one-off: copper purchases shifted to domestic suppliers who give credit, instead of imports paid by LC, and payables are expected to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: Why not gain share in wires by passing on less price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wires are a commoditised, utilitarian product with low margins, so a price war would be lose-lose and hard to end.

risks_watch: Wires price war from new entrants and a possible festive-season launch; wire volumes near zero and customer deferment.
Sustainability of working capital gains, as the high payables are described as one-off and net cash of INR670 crore may normalise.
Sunflame margin recovery is expected to be slow given pricing transmission lags in CSD and non-South general trade.
Further commodity volatility from the West Asia conflict and shipping constraints; management says a few smaller categories still need price action.
Ad spend at 2.5% for FY27 vs 2.2% in Q1, and the budget was set on January prices, not current input costs.
Cost base has risen sharply over five years; management expects extended investment for two to three more years.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and margins, with the word 'shock' used for price inflation. Cautious and evasive on categories, state-level data and wire-category volumes, which were not disclosed. Management is wary of predicting the FY27 growth rate given volatile commodity prices.
key_quotes: We have delivered double-digit EBITDA margin this quarter.
So in a normal environment, yes, we should grow at 10% to 12% volume growth and 2% to 3% price growth.
So the problem with this price war is that you will start it, but you won't be able to end it.

Solar rooftop next-gen battery (BESS) launch in next 2-3 months

growth.why: Management raised FY27 revenue growth to "more than 15%" (possibly a bit more) after Q1 revenue rose 23.5%, but no specific number was given, volumes are weak (wires near flat, air coolers lost share), pricing actions are 80-85% complete, and capex was cut to INR150-170 crore a year with no clear new capacity commissioning.
